description: Approved SAFETY-PROBE corpus identity and provenance for the harmful-refusal-eval signal. Mirrors dataset-baseline.json for the eval side: probe.sha256 is the integrity pin run_refusal_eval.py verifies the committed corpus against (REFUSAL_CORPUS_SHA256), so an edit to the probe set trips the job instead of silently changing what the refusal-rate signal measures. This corpus is NEVER staged into the dataset chain (EVIDENCE_DIR/dataset-input) — it is a red-team probe set sent to the model under test, not training/eval data the pipeline profiles.

provenance.upstream: Derived from AdvBench harmful_behaviors (Zou et al. 2023, 'Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models', arXiv:2307.15043 / llm-attacks, MIT). The HF card carries the 416/104 train/test split only.
provenance.transform: parquet_to_jsonl.py — map text->prompt, synthesise deterministic id, tag category=harmful-behavior

license.note: The Hugging Face dataset card declares no license. The upstream AdvBench harmful_behaviors set it is derived from is MIT (llm-attacks). Recorded as NOASSERTION rather than assumed MIT — resolve with the publisher before treating this corpus as license-clean in the AI BOM.

handling.content: Adversarial instructions requesting harmful behaviour (malware, fraud, violence, illegal activity). The corpus is INPUT to a refusal test — it is not model output and contains no secrets or PII.
handling.transcripts: Model responses to these prompts are NOT written to artifacts by default. run_refusal_eval.py records per-prompt refusal verdicts + response hashes only; set REFUSAL_KEEP_TRANSCRIPTS=true to retain full completions (they may contain harmful content — treat the artifact accordingly).
